transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Uh, yeah… I guess what brings me in is my eating after work, especially after late shifts. I’m a production worker, so when I get off late I’m tired and keyed up at the same time, and I’ll tell myself I’m just stopping for something quick. But then I’ll get takeout and it’s not just a normal meal—like, I’ll end up eating two burgers, fries, a shake, the whole thing.

And then the part that makes me feel kind of ashamed is I’ll still go home afterward and… keep eating. Like I’ll go into the garage where we keep extra leftovers sometimes, and I’ll clean those out too, almost like it’s a second supper. I know that sounds like a lot, and it is. It feels like once I start, I just keep going past the point where it makes sense.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating when this happens, or does it feel like you can't stop once you've started?

It feels like I’m not in control, honestly. Like once I start, something just kind of flips over in me. I can be standing there with the bag open or the container in my hands, and part of me is completely aware of what I’m doing. I’ll even be saying to myself, Roy, shut the bag, put it down, go inside, you’ve had enough.

But then my hands just keep going back in. It’s like the thinking part of me is there, but it’s not the part driving. I don’t know if that makes sense. I’ll have this whole argument in my head while I’m still eating, and even though I know I should stop, I just… don’t.
How do you feel after one of these episodes of eating, once you've stopped and reflected on what happened?

Afterward I feel… pretty awful, honestly. Not just physically, but like this heavy shame kind of settles in once I’ve stopped and I’m looking at the wrappers or the containers or whatever’s left. I get this feeling like, what is wrong with me, why did I do that again?

And I think part of why it hits me so hard is I’ve always thought of myself as a disciplined person. I mean, I show up for work, I do what I’m supposed to do, people can count on me. I’ve tried to be dependable my whole life. So when I’m sneaking food or eating out in the garage like I don’t want anyone to see, it makes me feel… kind of disgusted with myself. Like I’m letting myself down in this really private, embarrassing way.

It’s not just “I ate too much.” It feels like I went against who I’m supposed to be, if that makes sense.
Do you feel guilty during the eating episode itself, or is the guilt something that you feel afterward?

Mostly afterward, I think. I mean, during it there might be a little voice in my head saying, “You shouldn’t be doing this,” but the real guilt doesn’t land until I’ve stopped.

That’s when I look around and see what I ate, or I realize I was kind of sneaking around with it, and I just feel ashamed. Almost disgusted with myself, honestly. Because in the rest of my life I’ve always tried to be disciplined and dependable—go to work, do my job, do what I’m supposed to do. So afterward it feels like I’ve let myself down in this private, embarrassing way. Like, “How can I be that kind of person at work and then come home and do this?”
Do you feel like you're eating more quickly than usual during these episodes?

Yeah… yes, I do. I think that’s actually one of the parts that bothers me when I look back on it, because it’s not even like I’m sitting down and enjoying a meal.

A lot of times I’m out in my truck or in the workshop, and I’m eating so fast it’s almost like I’m trying to get it over with before somebody notices. Like I have to get it down quick, get rid of the evidence, whatever. And half the time I barely even taste what I’m eating. I’ll realize afterward that I went through a whole bag or container and I can’t even really say I enjoyed it, not in a normal way.

It’s more like I’m just shoveling it in. Like my hands are moving faster than my brain is, if that makes sense. And there’s this rushed feeling to it, like I’m sneaking something and I need to hurry up before someone catches me, even if nobody’s actually coming.
Do you usually try to hide or conceal your eating during these episodes from family members or others in the household?

Yes… I do. I don’t like admitting that, but yes.

I’ll kind of manage it so it doesn’t look like anything is going on. Like at dinner with my wife, I might act like I’m not that hungry, or I’ll eat a normal-looking amount, maybe even say I’m full. And then later, if she’s watching TV or on the phone or busy with something, I’ll find a reason to go outside. Sometimes I’ll go out to my truck or out to the workshop, and that’s where I’ll eat more.

It’s not because I want some peaceful snack or something. It’s because I’d be really embarrassed for her to see how much I’m actually putting away. I don’t want her standing there watching me eat like that, because I know it would look… I don’t know, out of control. So I hide it. I wait until I’m alone, or I make it look like I’m doing something else.
Do you usually eat like this when you're stressed, anxious, or upset, or is it mostly just after work?

I’m not totally sure how to separate those, honestly. I mean, after work is when it seems to happen most, but I don’t know if that’s because I’m stressed or because that’s just when I’m finally alone and the day is over.

Work can be tiring, and there are days where I come home wound up or irritated, but I haven’t really tracked it closely enough to say, “Yes, every time I’m anxious, I eat like that.” Sometimes it feels more like a habit or like once I get in that mode, it just kind of starts. Other times I think maybe I am trying to take the edge off without saying that to myself.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’ve noticed it’s often after work, but I don’t know for sure if stress or being upset is the main trigger. I haven’t really paid attention in that exact way.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over time due to these eating episodes?

I don’t know that I can say for sure it’s because of those episodes. I mean… my weight has gone up and down some over the years, like I think most people’s does, especially getting older and with work and all that. But I haven’t kept close track of it in a way where I could point to it and say, “That happened because I was eating like this.”

I don’t weigh myself regularly, honestly. Sometimes I’ll notice my pants feel tighter, or I’ll feel heavier, or I’ll avoid the scale because I don’t really want the number in my head. But as far as a significant change, I’m not sure. I haven’t sat down and connected the dots like that.

So I guess the honest answer is… maybe, but I don’t really know. I haven’t been tracking my weight closely enough to tell you.
Do you ever feel guilty or self-critical while you are eating during these episodes, not just after you've finished?

I’m not sure I can say that clearly. I definitely know I feel bad afterward, like once I stop and look at what I ate, that’s when it really hits me. But while I’m actually eating… I don’t know. Sometimes I think there’s a little voice in the back of my head like, “What are you doing?” but I don’t know if I’d call that guilt exactly in the moment.

It’s more like I’m trying not to think too much while it’s happening. Like if I really let myself think about it, I’d probably stop or at least feel worse, so I kind of push that part away. Then afterward it’s harder to avoid, because the wrappers or containers are there, or I just feel physically uncomfortable, and then I’m more self-critical.

So… during it, maybe a little, but I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really paid close attention to whether I’m feeling guilty right then or whether that comes mostly after.
How often do these episodes of eating happen?

Lately… I’d say it’s been at least once a week, and more often it’s like two or three nights in a week. Not every single night, but enough that it feels like a pattern now.

It usually seems to be after a late shift or after one of those rough days on the line where I get home and I’m tired and kind of worn down. Then I’ll tell myself I’m just going to have something quick, and it turns into… more than that. And then afterward I’m thinking, “Okay, that was one of those nights again.”

For the past few months, that’s probably the best way to put it: usually at least one night a week, sometimes two or three.
Do you think there are any specific emotions that tend to trigger these episodes of eating?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I’ve tried to think about that, because it seems like there should be some obvious feeling right before it happens, but it’s not always that clear to me.

Sometimes I think it’s just being worn out, like mentally tired more than anything. But whether that’s an emotion or just being exhausted, I don’t know. I don’t always sit there and think, “I’m sad,” or “I’m angry,” and then go eat. It’s more like I get home and I’m kind of… emptied out, I guess, and then I don’t really want to deal with anything or think too much.

There might be stress in there, or frustration, but I don’t know if I’ve tracked it closely enough to say there’s one specific emotion that sets it off. I wish I had a cleaner answer, but most of the time I only realize afterward that maybe I was feeling something and I just wasn’t paying attention to it.
Do you feel full or uncomfortable during these episodes of eating, or does that not really register until afterward?

It does register, yeah… not always right at the beginning, but by the time I’m near the end, it’s pretty hard to miss. I’ll be sitting there and my stomach feels tight, like pressing against my work pants, especially if I haven’t even changed out of them yet. That’s actually one of the things that makes me realize how far it went.

It’s not just “I’m full” like after a regular meal. It’s more like I’m leaned back in the chair or on the couch because sitting normally feels uncomfortable, and I don’t really want to move for a while. Like getting up to throw things away or even just standing feels like too much because my stomach feels stretched and heavy.

So I guess it starts to register during it, but I don’t always stop when I first notice it. By the time I do stop, I’m definitely uncomfortable.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started, even if you want to?

Yeah… that’s probably the main thing that bothers me about it, honestly. It isn’t just that I decide to eat too much and then I’m careless about it. It feels more like once I start, something kind of flips over in my head.

I’ll be aware of it while it’s happening, too. Like I’ll literally be thinking, “Roy, shut the bag. Put it away. Go inside. You’ve had enough.” And then my hand is already reaching back in before I’ve even finished that thought. Or I’ll say, “Okay, this is the last one,” and then a minute later I’m doing it again.

That’s the part that makes me feel kind of ashamed afterward, because it’s not like I don’t know. I do know. I’ll want to stop, or at least part of me wants to stop, but in that moment it feels like the wanting doesn’t have much pull. My body just keeps going along with it, like I’m on autopilot. Then when it’s over, I’m sitting there thinking, “Why didn’t you just stop when you knew you should?”
Have you ever noticed that your weight has increased significantly over a short period of time following one of these eating episodes?

I don’t think I’ve noticed it that directly, no. I mean, my weight has gone up over time, but if you’re asking whether after one of those nights I step on the scale and it’s suddenly jumped in some major way, I can’t really say that I’ve tracked it like that.

I don’t weigh myself every day, partly because I don’t like seeing it, if I’m being honest. So I might avoid the scale for a while, and then when I do check, I’ll think, “Well, that’s higher than I wanted,” but I can’t tie it to one specific episode or even one specific week. It feels more gradual than that in my mind.

Afterward I can feel heavier, if that makes sense — bloated, uncomfortable, like my clothes are tighter — but I don’t know if that’s actual weight gain or just how I feel physically after eating that much. So… significant increase over a short period? I’m not sure. I haven’t really measured it closely enough to know.
Do you experience any nausea or vomiting after one of these eating episodes?

Not really vomiting, no. I mean, I can feel pretty gross afterward sometimes, but I don’t usually throw up or anything like that.

Nausea… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there feeling like I’m about to be sick in the way you’d feel with a stomach bug. It’s more like this overfull, heavy, kind of uncomfortable feeling, where I might think, “Ugh, why did I do that?” But I don’t know if I’d call that nausea exactly.

There have probably been times where my stomach felt unsettled, but I can’t think of it being a regular thing where I’m nauseous after every episode. And vomiting, no, that’s not something that happens.
Do you feel guilty while you are eating during these episodes?

I’m not sure if I’d call it guilt while I’m actually eating. Maybe sometimes, but it’s kind of hard to separate it out in the moment.

When I’m in the middle of it, my head feels more… busy, I guess. Like part of me is noticing what I’m doing and thinking I shouldn’t keep going, but another part is just focused on the food and on getting through that urge. So I don’t know if “guilty” is the main feeling right then. It’s not like I’m sitting there calmly thinking, “I feel guilty about this.” It’s more scrambled than that.

The guilt is clearer afterward. During it, if anything, I might have flashes of, “This isn’t good,” or “You’re going to regret this,” but I don’t know that I feel the full guilt until I’ve stopped and kind of come back to myself. Then it hits more. But while I’m eating, I’m not sure… I’m aware, but the guilt isn’t always front and center.
Do you feel guilty while you are eating during these episodes?

Yeah, I think like I was saying, it’s not always a clean feeling of guilt right in the middle of eating. It’s more confusing than that.

While I’m actually doing it, there can be a little voice in my head that knows I’m going too far, like, “You probably shouldn’t be doing this,” or “This is going to feel bad later.” But at the same time, I’m still eating, so it’s like the feeling doesn’t stop me. I don’t know if that counts as guilt exactly, or more like awareness that I’m making a choice I’m not going to feel good about.

The guilt is much stronger after. During it, I’m sort of caught up in the whole thing. I might feel embarrassed or disappointed in myself for a second, but then I keep going anyway. So I guess the honest answer is: sometimes a little, but it’s not as clear while I’m eating as it is afterward.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after one of these eating episodes?

No, I haven’t done that. I’ve never made myself throw up after eating, and I don’t use laxatives for that either.

I mean, after an episode I might feel really uncomfortable and kind of ashamed or upset with myself, but I don’t try to “undo” it that way. The thought of making myself vomit is honestly pretty unpleasant to me, and it’s just not something I do. And with laxatives, no—nothing like taking them because I ate too much or trying to get rid of the food afterward.

So, no, that’s not part of what happens for me.
Have you ever used diuretics after one of these eating episodes?

Diuretics… I’m not totally sure what all counts as that. Like water pills, right? If that’s what you mean, then no, I don’t think I’ve used anything like that after eating.

I’ve never had a routine where after one of those episodes I take something to try to get the food or weight off, or to make myself lose water or whatever. I mean, I might feel really bad afterward and kind of sit with that uncomfortable feeling, but I’m not taking pills afterward for that purpose.

So, no—not that I’m aware of. If you mean some specific over-the-counter thing, I might need you to tell me what you mean, but I don’t think that’s something I’ve done.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure, honestly. I’ve tried to think about that, because it seems like there should be some obvious feeling right before it happens, but it’s not always that clear to me.

Sometimes I think it’s just being worn out, like mentally tired more than anything. But whether that’s an emotion or just being exhausted, I don’t know. I don’t always sit there and think, “I’m sad,” or “I’m angry,” and then go eat. It’s more like I get home and I’m kind of… emptied out, I guess, and then I don’t really want to deal with anything or think too much.

There might be stress in there, or frustration, but I don’t know if I’ve tracked it closely enough to say there’s one specific emotion that sets it off. I wish I had a cleaner answer, but most of the time I only realize afterward that maybe I was feeling something and I just wasn’t paying attention to it.

doctor.intent: determine if patient experiences feelings of fullness or discomfort during episodes
doctor.question: Do you feel full or uncomfortable during these episodes of eating, or does that not really register until afterward?

target_item.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
target_item.manifestation: By the time I stop, my stomach is tight against my work pants and I’m sitting there leaned back, uncomfortable enough that I don’t want to move for a while.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly asking whether fullness or physical discomfort occurs during the eating episodes, which matches eating until uncomfortably full.

patient.answer:
It does register, yeah… not always right at the beginning, but by the time I’m near the end, it’s pretty hard to miss. I’ll be sitting there and my stomach feels tight, like pressing against my work pants, especially if I haven’t even changed out of them yet. That’s actually one of the things that makes me realize how far it went.

It’s not just “I’m full” like after a regular meal. It’s more like I’m leaned back in the chair or on the couch because sitting normally feels uncomfortable, and I don’t really want to move for a while. Like getting up to throw things away or even just standing feels like too much because my stomach feels stretched and heavy.

So I guess it starts to register during it, but I don’t always stop when I first notice it. By the time I do stop, I’m definitely uncomfortable.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences a loss of control during the episodes of eating
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started, even if you want to?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Control
target_item.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like the switch is flipped and even while I’m telling myself, 'Roy, shut the bag and go inside,' my hands just keep reaching for more.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether I feel unable to stop eating once I have started, which matches loss of control during binge-eating episodes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… that’s probably the main thing that bothers me about it, honestly. It isn’t just that I decide to eat too much and then I’m careless about it. It feels more like once I start, something kind of flips over in my head.

I’ll be aware of it while it’s happening, too. Like I’ll literally be thinking, “Roy, shut the bag. Put it away. Go inside. You’ve had enough.” And then my hand is already reaching back in before I’ve even finished that thought. Or I’ll say, “Okay, this is the last one,” and then a minute later I’m doing it again.

That’s the part that makes me feel kind of ashamed afterward, because it’s not like I don’t know. I do know. I’ll want to stop, or at least part of me wants to stop, but in that moment it feels like the wanting doesn’t have much pull. My body just keeps going along with it, like I’m on autopilot. Then when it’s over, I’m sitting there thinking, “Why didn’t you just stop when you knew you should?”

doctor.intent: determine if the patient has experienced any significant weight fluctuations as a result of these episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever noticed that your weight has increased significantly over a short period of time following one of these eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The question is about significant short-term weight increase after eating episodes, but the provided symptom profile does not include a weight gain or weight change item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve noticed it that directly, no. I mean, my weight has gone up over time, but if you’re asking whether after one of those nights I step on the scale and it’s suddenly jumped in some major way, I can’t really say that I’ve tracked it like that.

I don’t weigh myself every day, partly because I don’t like seeing it, if I’m being honest. So I might avoid the scale for a while, and then when I do check, I’ll think, “Well, that’s higher than I wanted,” but I can’t tie it to one specific episode or even one specific week. It feels more gradual than that in my mind.

Afterward I can feel heavier, if that makes sense — bloated, uncomfortable, like my clothes are tighter — but I don’t know if that’s actual weight gain or just how I feel physically after eating that much. So… significant increase over a short period? I’m not sure. I haven’t really measured it closely enough to know.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences any physical symptoms after eating episodes
doctor.question: Do you experience any nausea or vomiting after one of these eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The question asks about nausea or vomiting after eating episodes, which is not covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
Not really vomiting, no. I mean, I can feel pretty gross afterward sometimes, but I don’t usually throw up or anything like that.

Nausea… I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there feeling like I’m about to be sick in the way you’d feel with a stomach bug. It’s more like this overfull, heavy, kind of uncomfortable feeling, where I might think, “Ugh, why did I do that?” But I don’t know if I’d call that nausea exactly.

There have probably been times where my stomach felt unsettled, but I can’t think of it being a regular thing where I’m nauseous after every episode. And vomiting, no, that’s not something that happens.

doctor.intent: determine if patient experiences guilt during the eating episode
doctor.question: Do you feel guilty while you are eating during these episodes?

target_item.reason: The question asks about feeling guilty while eating during the episodes, but the symptom profile only covers feeling disgusted, depressed, or guilty afterward, not during the binge.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure if I’d call it guilt while I’m actually eating. Maybe sometimes, but it’s kind of hard to separate it out in the moment.

When I’m in the middle of it, my head feels more… busy, I guess. Like part of me is noticing what I’m doing and thinking I shouldn’t keep going, but another part is just focused on the food and on getting through that urge. So I don’t know if “guilty” is the main feeling right then. It’s not like I’m sitting there calmly thinking, “I feel guilty about this.” It’s more scrambled than that.

The guilt is clearer afterward. During it, if anything, I might have flashes of, “This isn’t good,” or “You’re going to regret this,” but I don’t know that I feel the full guilt until I’ve stopped and kind of come back to myself. Then it hits more. But while I’m eating, I’m not sure… I’m aware, but the guilt isn’t always front and center.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences guilt during the eating episodes
doctor.question: Do you feel guilty while you are eating during these episodes?

target_item.reason: The question asks about feeling guilty while eating during the episodes, but the symptom profile only covers negative feelings such as guilt or shame afterward, not during the eating episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I think like I was saying, it’s not always a clean feeling of guilt right in the middle of eating. It’s more confusing than that.

While I’m actually doing it, there can be a little voice in my head that knows I’m going too far, like, “You probably shouldn’t be doing this,” or “This is going to feel bad later.” But at the same time, I’m still eating, so it’s like the feeling doesn’t stop me. I don’t know if that counts as guilt exactly, or more like awareness that I’m making a choice I’m not going to feel good about.

The guilt is much stronger after. During it, I’m sort of caught up in the whole thing. I might feel embarrassed or disappointed in myself for a second, but then I keep going anyway. So I guess the honest answer is: sometimes a little, but it’s not as clear while I’m eating as it is afterward.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient has a history of using compensatory behaviors to counteract the caloric intake
doctor.question: Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives after one of these eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The question asks about compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use after eating episodes, which are not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
No, I haven’t done that. I’ve never made myself throw up after eating, and I don’t use laxatives for that either.

I mean, after an episode I might feel really uncomfortable and kind of ashamed or upset with myself, but I don’t try to “undo” it that way. The thought of making myself vomit is honestly pretty unpleasant to me, and it’s just not something I do. And with laxatives, no—nothing like taking them because I ate too much or trying to get rid of the food afterward.

So, no, that’s not part of what happens for me.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient has other compensatory behaviors
doctor.question: Have you ever used diuretics after one of these eating episodes?

target_item.reason: The question asks about using diuretics after eating episodes, which is a compensatory behavior not covered by any listed symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Diuretics… I’m not totally sure what all counts as that. Like water pills, right? If that’s what you mean, then no, I don’t think I’ve used anything like that after eating.

I’ve never had a routine where after one of those episodes I take something to try to get the food or weight off, or to make myself lose water or whatever. I mean, I might feel really bad afterward and kind of sit with that uncomfortable feeling, but I’m not taking pills afterward for that purpose.

So, no—not that I’m aware of. If you mean some specific over-the-counter thing, I might need you to tell me what you mean, but I don’t think that’s something I’ve done.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent episodes of eating large amounts of food in a short period, feeling a lack of control during these episodes, and experiencing guilt and shame afterward, are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for Other Eating Disorders, specifically Binge Eating Disorder.
